title: The flagged prototype
promise: A clickable prototype where every PRD point is a switch, so a reviewer can turn each change on and off and see exactly what it does.
gives: One HTML file: a phone, a panel of switches numbered like the PRD, and a pin on every change.
clipTitle: A prototype you can *switch on and off*
clipLine: Every PRD point is a switch. Off is the product today.
when: A review keeps stalling on what a change would actually look like.
You want a yes or no on each change separately, not on the bundle.
You need to show the product as it is today next to the proposal.
skip: You need production UI. This is a sketch for deciding, not a design file.
The change has no screen, such as pricing logic or a backend rule.
You have not written the points down yet. Run the PRD skill first.

inputs.name: The PRD
inputs.note: `prd.json` from the PRD skill, or any list of numbered changes.

inputs.name: The screens today
inputs.note: Screenshots or a description of the current flow.

inputs.name: Brand basics
inputs.note: One colour and the product name are enough.

outputs.name: prototype.html
outputs.note: A single file that runs anywhere. No build step and no account.

outputs.name: A link per state
outputs.note: The address carries the screen and the switches, so you can send someone the exact comparison.

steps.title: Draw today first
steps.body: Every screen is built in its current state before anything is added, so off always means the product as it is.

steps.title: Add one switch per point
steps.body: Each switch carries its PRD number and a note that says what changes and why.

steps.title: Pin every change
steps.body: Anything a switch adds gets a numbered pin on the screen. Tap a pin to read its note.

steps.title: Make the path work
steps.body: The journey can be finished with any combination of switches. Controls outside the journey answer with a line that says what they would do.

steps.title: Add presets
steps.body: Today, the first release, and everything on, so a room can compare in one tap.

steps.title: Label what is made up
steps.body: Fictional data is marked on the first screen and in the panel.

checks.name: Every PRD point has a switch
checks.note: The checker compares the IDs in `prd.json` with the switches in the prototype.

checks.name: Every switch changes at least one screen
checks.note: Each screen is rendered with the switch off and on. Identical output fails.

checks.name: Every pin has a switch behind it
checks.note: A pin whose ID has no switch is an error, so pins and notes cannot drift apart.

checks.name: No dead taps
checks.note: Every control either navigates, acts or says what it would do.

checks.name: Any preset can finish the journey
checks.note: The checker walks the main path under each preset.

checks.name: Made-up data is labelled
checks.note: A disclosure has to appear in the panel.

checks.name: All switches off is the product today
checks.note: Compare the off state with your real screens before the review.

failures.title: It looks more finished than it is
failures.body: A phone frame makes anything look shippable, and reviewers start commenting on spacing.
failures.catch: Open the review by saying it is a sketch for deciding scope. The line at the bottom of the panel says the same.

failures.title: Switches interact
failures.body: Two changes can each be fine alone and crowded together.
failures.catch: Use the Everything preset early. If a screen breaks with all switches on, that is a finding for the PRD.

failures.title: Today drifts from the real product
failures.body: The off state is drawn from what you gave it. If your screenshots were old, so is the baseline.
failures.catch: Check the off state against the live app before anyone else sees it.

tangelo.label: Tangelo: the weekly shop
tangelo.note: Five screens and six switches on a phone. Take the tour, then drag the divider to compare today with the proposal.
tangelo.ask: Build the prototype for this PRD. One switch per point.
tangelo.demoNote: The agent reads the PRD, draws the app as it is today and wires one switch per point. Then a hand walks the tour, switch by switch, and drags a divider across the screen: today on the left, the proposal on the right. When the replay ends, the switches are yours.

run.by: A fresh agent session, given only the skill folder and a three-change brief for a different app (Kerb, a fictional parking app). Nobody answered its questions.
run.note: The sixth check compares switch IDs with a PRD, and this brief had none, so it ran in part. The run also found a bug in the checker and four gaps in the instructions. All are fixed in this version.
run.label: Open what it built

carousel.title: Everything off is *the product today*
carousel.body: The agent draws the app as it ships now. Nothing new is on the screen yet.

carousel.title: One switch is *one PRD point*
carousel.body: Turn on 1.1 and the reorder card appears on Home, with its number pinned to it.

carousel.title: Judge each change *on its own*
carousel.body: Three points are on. A reviewer can approve 1.1 and hold 3.1 without arguing about the whole design.

carousel.title: The numbers *follow you*
carousel.body: Tap through to the basket. The same IDs run from the PRD to the screen.

carousel.title: Checked *before* you see it
carousel.body: A script confirms every switch changes a screen you can reach, and that nothing new shows while it is off.

larkspur.label: Larkspur: share by link
larkspur.note: Four screens, two people and six switches, in a browser window. Take the tour: it walks the admin's side and the guest's.
larkspur.ask: Build the prototype for this PRD. One switch per point, and show both sides: the admin's and the guest's.
larkspur.demoNote: The agent reads the PRD, draws the app as it is today and wires one switch per point. Then the tour walks two browsers: Dana's, and the guest's. At the end a divider compares today with the proposal. When the replay ends, the switches are yours.

run.by: Built by hand as a reference example, then checked by the skill's script against the Larkspur PRD.
run.note: Building it found a gap in the checker: a change that lives only inside a dialog was not counted as a change. The script now reads dialogs as well as screens.

vireo.label: Vireo Recap: draft first, with sources
vireo.note: Three screens, two people and six switches, in a browser window. Turn on 1.1 and click a time: the recording plays from that moment.
vireo.ask: Build the prototype for this PRD. One switch per point. I want to click a line and hear where it came from.
vireo.demoNote: The agent reads the PRD, draws the recap as it is today and wires one switch per point. Then the tour clicks a time on a line and the recording plays from that moment. At the end a divider compares today with the proposal. When the replay ends, the switches are yours.

run.by: Built by hand as a reference example, then checked by the skill's script against the Vireo PRD.
run.note: The words of the meeting are invented to match the recap. The prototype shows the idea of a source on every line, not a working transcript.
